dedupe_keys.name: barmshour landfill shiraz predicting municipal solid waste slope behaviour with hybrid neural models

description: This case study predicts the mechanical behaviour of municipal solid waste layers for slope stability analysis at the Barmshour Landfill in Shiraz, Iran, where waste slopes face static and seismic loads. The authors, researchers at Isfahan University of Technology, Islamic Azad University Isfahan and Payame Noor University, trained four hybrid models that combine a multilayer perceptron with metaheuristic optimisers (BBO, MVO, VS and BSA) on measured data from the landfill, and published the work in an open-access journal article. Coverage is one landfill site. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence; the site data are not published. Caveats: results come from one site, the models are data-driven, not physically based, and the error values show sizeable scatter. The study found that the MVO-MLP model performed best, with a coefficient of determination of about 0.90 for both training and testing, and that hybrid models captured slope behaviour better than traditional approaches. Simulation uses: surrogate models for landfill slope failure under earthquake loading in waste infrastructure risk assessment. Related records: the Lahore and Rawalpindi landfill study (case_study-lahore-rawalpindi-landfill-methane-leachate-landgem) covers another aspect of landfill performance, and the EPA seismic design guidance for landfills (data-epa-rcra-subtitle-d-seismic-design-guidance-msw-landfills) sets the design context.
